summary: The AeroSANS Dashboard is a prediction-oriented, non-invasive Space Health solution for monitoring ONSD (Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter) patterns through ultrasound images. By leveraging the capabilities of automatic measurement, 3D biofeedback, and simulated cabin CO2 context data, it serves as an early detection mechanism for SANS (Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome).
details:
What it does and How it works

The AeroSANS is a non-invasive, digital Space Health Dashboard, which will allow the monitoring of the SANS condition. While conventional techniques require measurement of the ONSD through manual ultrasounds, we employ the 1-click “Auto-Measure” algorithm. Our technique utilizes classical image processing techniques and derives the ONSD in the B-mode ultrasound image in just a fraction of a second. Afterward, our system converts the raw 2-dimensional pixel information into a digital 3D reconstruction of the eye. The 3D optic nerve dynamically grows and changes its color (Green->Yellow->Red), according to the clinical threshold (5.0 mm & 5.7 mm). A simple click generates a complete medical PDF report for Mission Control telemetry.

The Creative Approach

Our innovation is in converting a complex and cryptic medical image into a user-friendly and holistic multisystem biofeedback panel. Not only did we design a medical calculator but we also incorporated environmental science in our design. The plotting of physiological ONSD trend values with simulated cabin CO₂ values on a dual axis graph gives a holistic situational awareness to the subject. Also, the conversion of 2D data into a 3D model would allow even non-medical trained astronauts to know about their health status.

Intended Impact & Benefits

For Space (Main Benefit): It will help preserve the vision of astronauts for the Artemis and Mars missions through its predictive and early warning system for ICP and optic disc edema before any irreversible injury happens.

For Earth (Dual Use Benefit): In addition to the deep space use, AeroSANS can also be deployed quickly in rural settings, battle fields or emergency rooms where the screening of traumatic brain injury and intracranial hypertension can be done easily and painlessly without invasive lumbar punctures.

Factors Our Team Considered

Clinical constraints and safety were of primary importance in our considerations. As a meta-analysis of 38 studies shows (Berhanu et al., 2023), ideal cut-offs for ONSD have a wide range of values. This is why our team made sure that AeroSANS would never provide a definite point diagnosis, but rather show trends longitudinally, taking into account an estimated ±0.3 mm error factor. Also, we took into account the absence of convection in microgravity, understanding that accumulated CO₂ after breathing out becomes a dangerous factor contributing to cerebral vasodilation.

Tools, Coding Languages, and Software Used

We created a complete Single Page Application (SPA) which runs without any backend services on a local offline spacecraft computer.

• Core Architecture: React and Vite (JavaScript).

• Image Processing: Custom deterministic algorithms written in pure JavaScript for edge detection, noise reduction, and RANSAC circle detection.

• 3D Visualization: Three.js for rendering the interactive 3D eyeball model and dynamic nerve swelling.

• Data Visualization: Chart.js (react-chartjs-2) for the dual-axis mission trend charts.

• Document Generation: jsPDF to compile and export the automated Earth-to-Orbit medical reports.
